source_text: Conuersus ibidem ad discipulos (uae' dicit auctori scan. dalorum: expedisse ei, si natus non fuisset aut si molino saxo ad collum deligato praecipitatus esset in profundum, quam unum ex illis modicis utique discipulis eius scandalizasset. aestima, quale supplicium comminetur ille. nec enim! alius ulciscetur scandalum discipulorum eius. agnosce igitur et iudicem et illo adfectu pronuntiantem de cura suorum, quo et creator retro: qui tetigerit uos, ac si pupillam oculi mei tangat. idem sensus eiusdem est. peccantem fratrem iubet corripi; quod qui non fecerit, utique deliquit, aut ex odio uolens fratrem in delicto perseuerare aut ex acceptione personae parcens ei: habes Leuiticum: non odies fratrem tuum in animo tuo, traductione traduces proximum tuum, utique et fratrem, et non sumes propter illum delictum. nec mirum, si ita docet qui pecora quoque fratris tui, si errantia in uia inueneris, prohibet despicias, quominus ea reducas fratri, nedum ipsum sibi.
pass_a_gloss: Having turned there to the disciples, He says to the author of scandals: it would have been better for him if he had not been born or if with a millstone of rock having been tied to his neck he had been thrown into the deep, than that he scandalized one of those little disciples of His. Estimate what kind of punishment He threatens. For not another will avenge the scandal of His disciples. Recognize, therefore, both the judge and Him pronouncing about the care of His own with that affection with which also the Creator formerly: he who touches you, as if he touches the pupil of my eye. The same sense is His. He commands to rebuke a sinning brother; which he who does not do, certainly has failed, either from hatred willing his brother to persist in the sin or from acceptance of persons sparing him. You have Leviticus: you shall not hate your brother in your heart, you shall not bring a curse upon your neighbor, certainly also not a brother, and you shall not take on account of him the sin. Nor is it wonderful, if He teaches thus, who also forbids you to despise the livestock of your brother, if you find them straying in the way, so that you may lead them back to your brother, much less himself to himself.

choices.english: you shall not take on account of him the sin
choices.why: Literal translation of the Latin phrase

choices.english: you shall not bring a curse upon your neighbor
choices.why: Correct interpretation of the Latin phrase
rejected: you shall surely rebuke your neighbor

bible_refs.note: you shall not hate your brother in your heart, you shall not bring a curse upon your neighbor

pass_b_english: Jesus turned to His disciples and issued a stern warning to anyone who would lead them astray: it would be better for that person to have never been born, or to have been thrown into the depths with a millstone around their neck, than to have caused one of His little disciples to stumble. The punishment He's threatening is severe - and it's not just any punishment, because God Himself will avenge the hurt done to His disciples. This is the same God who said, 'If anyone touches you, it's as if they're touching the pupil of my eye' (as the Creator had said). Jesus commands us to rebuke a brother who's sinning; if we don't, we're guilty of a failure, either because we hate our brother and want him to keep sinning, or because we're playing favorites and don't want to confront him. As it says in Leviticus (Leviticus 19:17-18), we're not to hate our brother in our heart, or bring a curse on our neighbor - and that includes our brother. In fact, we're not to hold their sin against them. It's no surprise Jesus teaches this way, since He also teaches us to care for our brother's livestock if we find it straying - how much more should we care for our brother himself? Jesus is emphasizing the importance of treating others with kindness and respect, and He will hold us accountable for our actions, so we must take His warnings seriously.

review.notes: Pass B adds significant content not present in the Locked Latin or Pass A, specifically the concluding sentence: 'Jesus is emphasizing the importance of treating others with kindness and respect, and He will hold us accountable for our actions, so we must take His warnings seriously.' This is an interpretive expansion rather than a translation. Additionally, Pass B includes an interpretation of 'nedum ipsum sibi' as 'how much more should we care for our brother himself' which, while capturing the sense, deviates from the literal structure of the source.
reasons: Pass B adds an entire concluding sentence of interpretation ('Jesus is emphasizing the importance of treating others with kindness and respect, and He will hold us accountable for our actions, so we must take His warnings seriously.') that is not found in the Locked Latin source.
